docs.title: About Me
docs.text:
I build the data foundations that make AI possible.

I’m a Principal Data Architect with more than 16 years of experience helping enterprises design and scale modern data platforms, cloud architectures, and AI-ready data ecosystems.

My work spans data engineering, distributed computing, enterprise architecture, cloud transformation, and strategic AI enablement. I help organizations turn complex data environments into dependable, secure, and high-performing foundations for analytics and GenAI adoption.

Currently, I help drive Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy for Data and AI. I focus on translating complex technical capabilities into scalable, revenue-generating business solutions for enterprise clients.

I partner with business and technology leaders to translate technical capability into measurable commercial value—bridging data strategy, platform design, and operational execution across modern enterprise environments.

Strategic Leadership & C-Suite Advisory: My focus extends beyond technical execution to delivering measurable enterprise business value. I partner with C-suite and VP-level stakeholders to navigate AI governance, maximize ROI, design scalable operating models, and manage data/AI risk. By bridging the gap between complex data engineering and strategic business goals, I ensure that data platforms actively drive revenue, operational efficiency, and competitive advantage.

Core expertise: Data Architecture | Data Engineering | Cloud Platforms | Apache Spark | PySpark | AWS | Azure | GCP | Databricks | Snowflake | Microsoft Fabric | Data Migration | Generative AI | AI-ready Data Platforms

docs.title: Avixa – Enterprise Data Modernization & Analytics Platform
docs.text: Role: Data Architect / Lead Engineer Domain: Audio-Visual Industry Association (Non-Profit / Membership) Tech Stack: Microsoft Fabric, Azure Data Lake (OneLake), Power BI, Apache Spark, SQL, Salesforce, Sage Intacct, Pardot

docs.title: 🎯 Project Overview
docs.text:
AVIXA, the global association for the audio-visual industry, faced challenges with fragmented data silos across their CRM (Salesforce), ERP (Sage Intacct), and marketing automation (Pardot) systems. As the Data Architect / Lead Engineer, I led the "Fabric POV" initiative to modernize their data estate.

The goal was to build a unified analytics platform that could accurately measure Customer Value, Sales Performance (from pipeline to recognized revenue), and Audience Engagement (from prospect to member).

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture & Implementation
docs.text:
I architected a Microsoft Fabric Data Lakehouse utilizing a Medallion Architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold) to ensure data quality, scalability, and clear separation of concerns.

Figure 1: End-to-end data flow from Source Systems through the Medallion Architecture to Power BI Consumption.

  • Data Ingestion (Bronze): Built automated pipelines to ingest raw data from Salesforce (Accounts, Opportunities), Sage Intacct (Financials), and Pardot (Audience/Leads) into OneLake.
  • Transformation (Silver): Implemented data cleansing, deduplication, and standardization logic using Spark notebooks. This included creating a unified "Audience" dataset merging Leads, Contacts, and Pardot prospects.
  • Modeling (Gold): Designed domain-specific semantic models for three core business areas:
    1. Value of Customer: Tracking growth across segments (Broadcast AV, IT, Education) and monitoring Tier 1A account movement.
    2. Sales Performance: Creating an end-to-end view from Pipeline → Contracted → Recognized Revenue, ensuring alignment between CRM and ERP within a ±2% tolerance.
    3. Audience Engagement: Profiling digital and event engagement to measure conversion rates from audience to paying customer.

docs.title: 🚀 DevOps & Governance
docs.text:
To ensure enterprise-grade reliability, I established a robust CI/CD and governance framework mapped directly to Microsoft Fabric capacities.

Figure 2: Multi-workspace DevOps strategy mapping Git branches to Fabric capacities.

  • 3-Tier Workspace Strategy: Mapped Git branches (Dev → Release → Main) to dedicated Dev, Test, and PROD workspaces.
  • CI/CD Pipelines: Implemented automated deployment pipelines to promote notebooks, data pipelines, and lakehouse artifacts from Dev Capacity to Prod Capacity securely.
  • Data Governance: Defined strict "Source of Truth" rules: Salesforce for CRM data, Sage Intacct for Revenue, and Pardot for Engagement metrics.

docs.title: 📊 Business Impact
docs.text:
• Unified Reporting: Delivered three executive-level Power BI dashboards replacing manual, fragmented Excel-based reporting.
  • Forecast Accuracy: Improved revenue forecasting by aligning Salesforce pipeline data with Sage Intacct recognized revenue.
  • Strategic Insight: Enabled leadership to track "Treat As" tier overrides and segment-specific growth (e.g., emerging markets vs. legacy Broadcast AV).

docs.text:

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Architected and led the delivery of an enterprise-grade, multi-source real estate data integration platform for CrossCountry Mortgage (CCM). Designed a resilient, incremental ETL pipeline ingesting millions of MLS (Multiple Listing Service) records from Tier-1 data vendors. Translated complex real estate market rules into scalable data models, culminating in a dual-layer NoSQL aggregation engine that powers real-time Loan Officer prospecting, automated loan alerts, and advanced realtor performance analytics.

Study Area: CrossCountry Mortgage (CCM) - US Mortgage & Real Estate Operations Duration: [Insert Start Year] – Present Role: Project Lead & Data Architect Status: Active / Production

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture
docs.text: The platform utilizes a serverless, event-driven hybrid cloud architecture to ingest heterogeneous data (S3 file drops and Snowflake warehouse views), process it through distributed Spark jobs, and serve it via optimized NoSQL document stores.

docs.title: Key Components
docs.text:
• Data Sources: ATTOM (File-based), CoreLogic (Snowflake JWT-secured views), CCM CRM (Monitored Properties)
  • Orchestration Layer: AWS Step Functions for idempotent, state-managed incremental ETL
  • Processing & Warehousing: AWS Glue (PySpark), Amazon Redshift (MERGE/UPSERT strategies)
  • Address Standardization: Smarty API integration with SHA-256 canonical hashing
  • NoSQL Aggregation Layer: MongoDB (Nested profile documents & Flat yearly documents)

docs.title: ⚙️ Cloud-Native Incremental ETL Architecture
docs.text: The platform leverages AWS Step Functions and Glue to ensure exactly-once processing semantics, enabling safe pipeline retries and resume-from-failure capabilities.

docs.title: Architecture Components
docs.text:
• Watermarking Engine: Dynamic extraction of MAX(SOURCE_DATETIME_UTC) to fetch only delta changes from Snowflake via JWT key-pair authentication.
  • Folder-Level Deduplication: S3 prefix scanning and Redshift log-table checks to ensure idempotent file processing.
  • Parallel Branching: Concurrent execution of downstream Loan Alert APIs and Unique Realtor matching workflows upon successful primary record designation.
  • Circuit Breakers: Automated data-volume guardrails to prevent runaway API storms caused by upstream data anomalies.

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text:
• ATTOM MLS Data: Tab-delimited property listings, parcel-matched addresses, and agent-entered details.
  • CoreLogic MLS Data: Snowflake-hosted assessor-level situs addresses and standardized status category codes.
  • CCM CRM Data: Loan-to-property watchlists for automated Loan Officer alerting.
  • External Address Validation: Smarty Streets API for canonical address standardization and geocoding.

docs.title: ETL Processing Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Ingest: Pull delta records from S3 or Snowflake using dynamic watermarking.
  2. Transform & Deduplicate: Apply the "15-Day Market Event Isolation Rule" to identify canonical "Primary Listing Records".
  3. Standardize: Compute SHA-256 address hashes, route to Smarty API, and enforce retry cooldowns for unresolved addresses.
  4. Aggregate: Roll up closed transactions into dual-mode MongoDB documents (Nested for trends, Flat for faceted search).
  5. Trigger: Match active primary listings against CRM watchlists and dispatch real-time Loan Alerts via REST API.

docs.title: Tools & Technologies
docs.text: Tool Purpose AWS Step Functions Serverless orchestration of incremental ETL workflows AWS Glue (PySpark) Distributed data processing and complex business logic Amazon Redshift Staging, MERGE/UPSERT operations, and workflow state tracking Snowflake Secure, JWT-authenticated extraction of CoreLogic delta data MongoDB Dual-schema NoSQL storage for realtor profiles and aggregations Smarty API Third-party address validation, standardization, and geocoding SHA-256 Hashing Canonical address key generation for cross-vendor property matching

docs.title: ATTOM & CoreLogic Incremental Pipelines
docs.text: Designed two distinct but harmonized ingestion pipelines. The ATTOM pipeline handles S3 file drops with folder-level deduplication, while the CoreLogic pipeline queries Snowflake views using JWT key-pair authentication. Both converge on a shared address standardization layer and business logic engine.

docs.title: Realtor Data Aggregation (Nested & Flat Models)
docs.text: Architected a dual-write aggregation pipeline. The Nested Model stores complete lifecycle data, rolling windows (3M/6M/12M), and YoY growth percentages for deep trend analysis. The Flat Model de-normalizes annual summaries into standalone documents (1 Realtor + 1 Year = 1 Document) to eliminate expensive $unwind operations for front-end faceted search.

docs.title: Loan Alert & Prospecting Engine
docs.text: Built an event-driven alerting system that matches newly active primary listings against a CRM-sourced "Monitored Properties" watchlist. Implemented tiered suppression rules (e.g., do not alert if sent within 15 days) and safety caps to protect the external REST API from runaway data anomalies.

docs.title: 🏆 Key Results & Impact
docs.text:
• Performance: Eliminated full-table scans via incremental watermarking, reducing compute costs by 80%
  • Accuracy: Implemented the 15-Day Deduplication Algorithm to filter out MLS data corrections and amendments
  • UX Optimization: Flat MongoDB schema reduced front-end query latency for faceted search by avoiding array unwinds
  • Reliability: Achieved exactly-once processing semantics with idempotent, resume-safe pipeline design

docs.title: Technical Achievements
docs.text:
• Designed the "15-Day Market Event Isolation Rule" in distributed Spark logic to accurately distinguish genuine property sales from backend MLS data corrections.
  • Implemented asynchronous, batched address standardization with SHA-256 hashing and retry cooldowns, optimizing third-party API costs.
  • Built a unified address dimension model enabling seamless property matching across disparate MLS data feeds from multiple vendors.
  • Led cross-functional delivery, acting as the technical bridge between Data Engineering, Product, and CCM’s downstream application teams.

docs.title: Challenge 1: Volatile MLS Data & Duplicate Market Events
docs.text: Problem: MLS data is highly volatile. A single property sale might have multiple "Sold" records due to backend system corrections, or an "Active" listing might overlap with a pending sale, causing duplicate prospecting alerts. Solution: Developed a custom sorting and windowing algorithm in Spark. Records are partitioned by Property ID and sorted by effective_date. The algorithm enforces that two "Sold" events are only treated as distinct market events if they are ≥ 15 days apart.

docs.title: Challenge 2: High-Performance Faceted Search in NoSQL
docs.text: Problem: The prospecting application required high-performance filtering (e.g., "Show me all realtors in Texas ranked in the Top 50 in 2024"). Querying a deeply nested MongoDB document for year-specific metrics required expensive $unwind and $group aggregations. Solution: Architected a secondary "Flat" MongoDB collection. By de-normalizing the annual summary array into standalone, top-level scalar documents, we reduced front-end query latency significantly, directly improving the UX for Loan Officers.

docs.title: Challenge 3: Third-Party API Rate Limiting & Costs
docs.text: Problem: Submitting millions of raw, inconsistently formatted real estate addresses to the Smarty API would incur massive costs and trigger rate-limiting blocks. Solution: Implemented a canonical SHA-256 address hashing mechanism. Before calling the API, the pipeline checks a local hash mapping table. Only truly unique, unresolved addresses are batched and sent to the API, with a built-in cooldown period for previously failed validations.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Engineered enterprise-scale ETL and data warehouse solutions for Fortune 100 insurer Nationwide, integrating 48+ disparate source systems into a centralized 100+ Terabyte Teradata platform supporting ~85% of business analytics and regulatory reporting.

Study Area: Nationwide Insurance Enterprise (US Operations) Duration: August 2010 – August 2016 Role: Senior System Engineer (IBM India Pvt Ltd) Status: Completed

docs.title: ️ Architecture
docs.text: The enterprise data warehouse integrated multiple source systems through a robust ETL layer into a centralized Teradata platform.

docs.title: Key Components
docs.text:
• Source Systems (48+): Policy Admin, Claims, Billing, CRM Portal, and 44+ additional systems
  • ETL Layer: FastLoad, MultiLoad, FastExport for high-performance data movement
  • Teradata EDW (100+ TB): Centralized data warehouse with multiple data marts
  • Business Users: Compliance, Risk, Finance, and Smart Ride analytics teams

docs.title: ⚙️ Teradata MPP Architecture
docs.text: The platform leveraged Teradata's Massively Parallel Processing (MPP) architecture for high-performance query execution.

docs.title: Architecture Components
docs.text:
• Parsing Engine (PE): SQL request processing, session management, query optimization
  • BYNET Interconnect: High-speed communication fabric between PE and AMPs
  • Access Module Processors (AMPs): Parallel execution engines with local storage
  • Shared-Nothing Design: Each AMP processes its local data independently

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text:
• Policy Administration Systems: Legacy mainframes (AS/400) and modern systems (Duck Creek/Guidewire)
  • Claims Management Systems: Open/closed claims, adjuster notes, payout tracking
  • Billing & Invoicing Systems: Premium collections, agent commissions, payment gateways
  • CRM & Agent Portals: Salesforce and custom web portals for quotes and policy binding
  • External Third-Party Data: MVR (DMV records), credit scores (ISO/Verisk), weather data
  • Finance & HR Systems: SAP/Oracle for statutory accounting and payroll

docs.title: ETL Processing Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Extract: Pull data from 48+ source systems using FastLoad for initial loads
  2. Transform: Apply business rules, data validation, and SCD Type 2 logic
  3. Load: Use MultiLoad for incremental updates to non-empty tables
  4. Export: FastExport for downstream system feeds and regulatory reporting
  5. Validate: Exception handling and error routing for data quality issues

docs.title: Tools & Technologies
docs.text: Tool Purpose Teradata Enterprise data warehouse platform (100+ TB) FastLoad High-speed loading of empty target tables MultiLoad Incremental loads and updates to non-empty tables FastExport Large-volume data extraction for downstream systems SQL/Stored Procedures Complex transformations and business logic Unix Shell Scripting Job automation, SFTP transfers, and orchestration SCD Type 2 Historical tracking of policy and customer changes

docs.title: Commercial Velocity
docs.text: Built data pipelines to accelerate the quote-to-bind process for commercial insurance, enabling agents to issue policies in minutes instead of days. Integrated underwriting rules and pricing models into the data warehouse.

docs.title: Smart Ride & TTS (Telematics)
docs.text: Developed ETL workflows for Nationwide's usage-based insurance program. Processed high-volume telematics data (driving behavior, mileage, hard braking events) to calculate risk scores and customer discounts.

docs.title: Compliance & Regulatory Reporting
docs.text: Engineered data marts for Finance and Risk teams to produce accurate statutory reports required by NAIC (National Association of Insurance Commissioners) and state insurance regulators.

docs.title: Key Results & Impact
docs.text:
• Performance: Optimized nightly batch processing to meet 4-hour SLA window for mission-critical reporting
  • Scale: Successfully integrated 48+ source systems into unified 100+ Terabyte data warehouse
  • Coverage: Platform supported ~85% of Nationwide's business analytics operations
  • Quality: Implemented robust validation framework reducing data errors in compliance reports

docs.title: Technical Achievements
docs.text:
• Reduced batch processing time by 20% through SQL optimization and proper use of Teradata utilities
  • Implemented SCD Type 2 logic to track historical changes in policy addresses and risk factors
  • Built exception handling framework that routed invalid records to error tables instead of failing entire batches
  • Automated job orchestration using Unix shell scripts with email alerts for failed jobs

docs.title: Challenge 1: Data Quality from Legacy Systems
docs.text: Problem: Source data from legacy mainframes had missing Policy IDs and inconsistent date formats. Solution: Implemented robust data validation checks in the staging layer. Invalid records were routed to exception tables for manual review, preventing batch failures.

docs.title: Challenge 2: Meeting Strict SLA Windows
docs.text: Problem: Nightly batch jobs needed to complete within 4 hours to deliver data by 8 AM for business users. Solution: Optimized SQL queries, collected statistics on join columns to avoid product joins, and used MultiLoad for efficient incremental updates.

docs.title: Challenge 3: High-Volume Telematics Data
docs.text: Problem: Smart Ride generated massive amounts of driving behavior data daily. Solution: Designed scalable ETL pipelines using FastLoad for initial loads and implemented data aggregation logic to reduce storage requirements.

docs.title: Thrive TRM — Enterprise SaaS Data Migration & Validation Platform
Role
docs.text: Data Quality Engineer / Migration Validation Lead

docs.title: Client
docs.text: Thrive TRM — Talent Relationship Management platform for executive search firms

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Thrive TRM is a multi-tenant SaaS platform serving executive search firms, managing 1.2M+ executives, 193K+ companies, and 99K+ candidate-job relationships. The platform underwent a major architectural migration from a legacy per-tenant database schema (T1) to a consolidated multi-tenant architecture (T2 / Phoenix), impacting 270+ enterprise customers.

docs.title: The Challenge
docs.text: Migrating 270+ customers across 134+ tables with zero data loss was non-negotiable. The structural differences between T1 and T2 were significant — schema renames, normalized tables, derived fields, and value-map transformations meant that simple row-count checks were insufficient. Every field had to be validated at the record level before go-live.

docs.title: Architecture & Approach
docs.text:
Built an automated validation engine using Python + PostgreSQL Foreign Data Wrappers (FDW):

  • FDW Bridge: T2 database reads T1 data directly through fdw_{tenant} schemas — no data copies, no SSM tunnels, matching production deployment posture.
  • 134 Table Query Pairs: Each pair contains a T1 SQL (reading through FDW) and a T2 SQL (reading native tables), both returning a match_key + comparable fields.
  • Smart Match Keys: Preserved IDs for global tables, transformed natural keys for customer-scoped tables, import_key for migrated records — mirroring the migration SQL's own strategy.
  • Value Normalization: Recursive normalization of JSON, arrays, whitespace, and NULL handling to avoid false-positive mismatches.
  • Incremental Reporting: JSON + Markdown + HTML reports generated per-tenant, with progress checkpoints for resumable runs.

docs.title: Key Technical Highlights
docs.text:
• Field-level diffing across 134+ tables including complex domains: candidacies, scorecards, custom fields, GDPR consents, and LinkedIn-enriched data.
  • Value-map mirroring: Validation queries replicate the exact migration transforms (e.g., 100+ row veteran/disability status maps, seniority level mappings, event type resolution) to ensure apples-to-apples comparison.
  • Tenant isolation verification: Patch runs fingerprint every other tenant's tables before/after to guarantee no cross-tenant data leakage.
  • Schema drift analysis: Tooling to compare all 270+ T1 schemas and identify structural divergence before migration.

docs.title: Measurable Impact
docs.text:
• Zero-defect go-lives for every tenant migration across 270+ customers.
  • 1.2M+ people records and 193K+ company records validated with field-level precision.
  • 99K+ candidacy relationships verified through complex pipeline state migrations.
  • Incremental reports enabled parallel migration waves without blocking.

docs.title: Technologies
docs.text: Python, PostgreSQL, AWS RDS, FDW (Foreign Data Wrapper), Pandas, AWS CLI/IAM, Jupyter, GitHub Actions, PyTest, Make, Docker

  • table_specs.py — 134+ T1/T2 query pair specifications
  • valid.py — Production migration validator (ported to notebook)
  • schema_drift_analyzer — Cross-tenant schema comparison tool
  • migration_validator — Standalone post-migration deep-dive utility
